chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: concerning

A woman drank medicine while she was pregnant in order to cast out her child, and she expelled her child. He said: “If it had bone and flesh had grown upon it, and hearing and sight had been opened for it, then its blood-money is upon her, which she gives to its father.” He said: “And if it was a fetus, a clot, or a morsel of flesh, then forty dinars or a ghurrah are upon her, which she gives to its father.” I said: So she does not inherit from her child’s blood-money? He said: “No, because she killed him.”

And this interpretation does not conflict with the narration of al-Halabi and Abi 'Ubaydah that the woman was in labor, because it is not impossible that she was in labor even if the child had not reached full development when it was a miscarriage; therefore, there is no objection on any account.

key_terms.تَرِثُ: inherits; receives inheritance from the deceased
key_terms.حَامِلٌ: pregnant; describing the woman carrying a child
key_terms.دَوَاءً: medicine taken to induce expulsion of the fetus
key_terms.دِيَتَهُ: his blood-money; the financial compensation due for the fetus
key_terms.غُرَّةً: a specified indemnity payment in fetal injury cases

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on blood-money if a pregnant woman causes the miscarriage of her fetus?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a pregnant woman who deliberately causes the loss of her fetus. It specifies different amounts of blood-money according to the stage of fetal development and rules that the mother does not inherit from the blood-money because she caused the killing.
